advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep census with a behavioral assertion (drive each writer/transport and assert the emitted label value) or justify it as a structural manifest rather than a code grep.
advisory.finding: test_the_writer_emits_the_COLON_label_form_and_nothing_emits_the_hyphen asserts by grepping the SOURCE TEXT of production modules (binding_recovery.py, dispatch_one.py, apply_inbound_records.py) for the implementation literal f"rebar-id:{local_id}". This is source-grepping the code under test: a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. extracting the label format into a helper such as _rebar_label(local_id)) would flip the assertion red with no observable-behavior change. This diff actively edits the census (retargeting the third writer to binding_recovery.py), so the coupling is re-affirmed here rather than merely inherited.
scenarios: A future refactor factors the rebar-id label literal into a shared constant/helper; behavior is unchanged but this census goes red.
A writer keeps emitting the colon label via a helper call rather than the inline f-string; the grep no longer finds the literal and misreports the writer as gone.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting binding_store._INDEX_LAG_GRACE_SECONDS/_MISSES_BEFORE_UNBIND/_age_seconds are identical to their binding_recovery counterparts.
evidence: comment: 'Rebinding either constant here would desynchronize it from the recovery that actually enforces it'
ABSENCE: test_binding_recovery.py exercises the recovery-owned constants directly but contains no assertion tying the binding_store aliases to the binding_recovery source of truth.
advisory.finding: binding_store.py rebinds _INDEX_LAG_GRACE_SECONDS, _MISSES_BEFORE_UNBIND and _age_seconds as ALIASES of binding_recovery's definitions, and the diff's own comment warns that rebinding either constant would silently desynchronize the facade's inspection surface from the recovery that enforces it. No test in this change asserts binding_store._INDEX_LAG_GRACE_SECONDS is binding_recovery._INDEX_LAG_GRACE_SECONDS (etc.), so a future accidental re-definition of the constant in binding_store.py — the exact failure the comment fears — would pass unnoticed.
scenarios: A later edit re-introduces a literal grace value in binding_store.py; the aliased monkeypatch-based oracles then freeze the wrong value and duplicate-prevention behavior silently changes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the ABORT_REPLACE_FAILED abort's evidence carries the error string and the affected jira_key/local_id.
evidence: test at tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_recovery.py:607-622 asserts only '[a.reason for a in outcome.aborted] == [ABORT_REPLACE_FAILED]' and disk state, not a.evidence
ABSENCE: no assertion that the ABORT_REPLACE_FAILED abort's evidence contains the error or the affected identities.
advisory.finding: The replace-failure path builds RetirementAbort evidence containing an 'error': repr(exc) field, but test_a_live_replace_failure_retains_the_overlap_and_aborts asserts only the abort reason and the preserved disk/memory state — it never asserts the abort's evidence carries the error/identity payload. The general evidence-carrying contract is tested only for the classifier mismatch path (test_an_abort_carries_the_evidence_a_human_needs), leaving the ABORT_REPLACE_FAILED evidence assembly unverified.
scenarios: A regression drops or mis-populates the error/identity evidence on a replace-failure abort; the operator report loses the detail it was designed to carry and no test fails.
